second_order: working out where and how to build flags and menorahs
theme_note: These codes all do the practical work of starting, locating, placing, sizing, and redesigning shared symbols; what varies is the symbol, site, and whether the turn calls, corrects, places, or reports progress.

second_order: guarding and repairing the flags and menorah
theme_note: These passages organize or perform continued protection and repair after work exists; they vary from urgent calls and maintenance reports to rebuilding, staying, or abandoning a damaged object.

second_order: reporting attacks, damage, and who did it
theme_note: These codes name damage, attacks, losses, or attributed attackers rather than carrying out the defence itself; certainty and attribution vary within the group.

second_order: negotiating whether to take or share canvas space
theme_note: These codes contest how space may be used: proposing overwrites, objecting, moving, compromising, limiting borders, or repairing neighbours. They vary between attack proposals, restraint, and accepted bargains.

second_order: trading pixel help and protection with neighbours
theme_note: These passages ask for, promise, give, or reciprocate help and protection across named groups; what varies is whether the exchange is an alliance, a single pixel, mutual watching, or a later relationship.

second_order: concentrating canvas coordination in Discord and the megathread
theme_note: These codes move people, projects, and instructions into shared organizing threads or Discord, including invitations, explanations, redirects, and moderation; what varies is the venue and who directs the move.

second_order: joking and taking Israeli pride in the pixel fight
theme_note: These passages turn canvas action into locally inflected jokes, historical-political wordplay, or declarations of Israeli pride; the specific joke and whether it accompanies building or guarding vary.

second_order: asking and explaining what the canvas shows
theme_note: These codes make the shared work legible by asking what words, designs, or activity maps show and answering from the record; what is interpreted varies.

second_order: celebrating, mourning, and recounting the pixel work
theme_note: These passages collectively mark results and tell what the effort became, varying between progress celebration, loss, survival, apology, exhaustion, and retrospective storytelling.

second_order: reviving the room's own April Fools jokes
theme_note: These codes stage the subreddit’s separate April Fools conduct by reviving the circle-jerk format or launching the Dead Sea fishermen petition joke; they are not treated as canvas conduct.

second_order: using r/place to judge online organization
theme_note: This single code uses the canvas as a measure of online organization and belongs with no other practice in the pool.

second_order: trying and refusing another pixel canvas
theme_note: These turns answer the finished event by recruiting a replacement canvas and declining it because once a year was enough or it was not Reddit; the proposal and refusals are one visible practice of deciding whether to repeat it.
